key_insight: For normalized gradient descent on convex Hölder-smooth objectives, the last iterate converges more slowly than the best/averaged iterate under a constant stepsize, but a linearly decreasing stepsize removes the logarithmic gap.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical stepsize rule for optimization systems that report the final model iterate, especially when only weak smoothness assumptions are available.
method: Analyze last-iterate convergence of normalized gradient descent for convex (ν,Mν)-Hölder-smooth objectives.
Prove a constant-stepsize bound of O((log^2(T)/T)^((1+ν)/2)) for the final iterate.
Show that a linearly decreasing stepsize achieves O(T^(-(1+ν)/2)) without needing ν or Mν.
evidence_signal: The paper combines theory with finite-horizon worst-case numerical study via the performance estimation problem (PEP) to test whether the logarithmic overhead is intrinsic.
watch_item: The improved rate uses a decreasing stepsize, so performance may depend on horizon-aware tuning and may be less convenient than a single fixed stepsize.
paper_title: Last-Iterate Convergence Rate of Normalized Gradient Descent under Hölder Smoothness
